title: Ethiopian Broad Bean Stew
community: All of Ethiopia — the broad bean fasting stew
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Broad Bean Stew — dried broad beans (fava beans) soaked and slow-cooked in a berbere sauce. A substantial, filling fasting stew — broader in flavour than lentils, with the distinctive earthiness of fava beans absorbing the berbere.
longDesc: Broad bean stew is an important part of Ethiopia's legume-based fasting cuisine — the fava bean's earthy, slightly meaty flavour makes it one of the most satisfying fasting proteins available.
ingredients: 2 cups dried broad beans (fava beans) — soaked overnight, outer skins removed
steps: Remove outer skins from soaked beans.
Add oil and berbere. Fry 3 minutes.
Add cooked beans with some cooking liquid.
chefTips: Remove the outer skins after soaking — they cause digestive discomfort.
The beans should remain whole but be very tender.
cookingScience: Fava beans contain vicine and convicine — compounds that can cause digestive problems (and haemolytic anaemia in G6PD-deficient individuals). Removing the outer skins and boiling reduces these compounds dramatically.
sustainabilityTips: Broad beans are nitrogen-fixing — one of the most sustainable legumes.
healthBenefits: L-dopa content may support neurological health.
culturalNote: Broad bean stew is one of Ethiopia's most ancient fasting foods — fava beans were among the earliest cultivated plants in the Ethiopian highlands, and their use in fasting cuisine connects to agricultural traditions thousands of years old.
